title: Fast and slow
summary: Hear the speed words and speed changes, and learn the Italian terms that name them.

hook.text: Many pieces end by slowing down, as if the music is running out of battery. Press play and watch the cursor. Where does this tune start to slow? What does the page tell you?

explore.text: Press play: the tune starts steady, speeds up, then slows at the end. Now pick one key and tap it. Start with a slow, steady walk, then speed up a little with every tap, then slow down again.
explore.goal: Play the clip, then tap a key: slowly, faster and faster, then slower and slower.

cards.text: Speed words are Italian and sit above the first [[bar|bar]]. They tell you the [[tempo|tempo]]. [[lento|Lento]] is slow. [[adagio|Adagio]] is slow and calm. [[andante|Andante]] is a walking pace. This tune is marked *Adagio*: press play.

Faster: [[moderato|moderato]] is a moderate speed, [[allegretto|allegretto]] is quite quick and [[allegro|allegro]] is quick and lively. [[poco|Poco]] means a little and [[molto|molto]] means very much, so *molto allegro* is very quick. Same tune, now marked *Allegro*.

Speed can change inside a piece. [[accelerando|Accelerando]] (*accel.*) means gradually faster. [[ritardando|Ritardando]] (*rit.*) and [[rallentando|rallentando]] (*rall.*) mean gradually slower. [[a-tempo|A tempo]] snaps back to the speed before. Listen for the slowing, then the return.

alternative.text: Picture a bike ride. You push off slowly, then pedal faster and faster: [[accelerando|accelerando]]. At the end you ease off and roll to a stop: [[ritardando|ritardando]]. Press play and follow the words above the notes.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **allegro**?
questions.hint: Allegro is quick and lively. Tap along: which clip makes you tap faster?

options.reason: Clip A is slow, about one beat a second. [[allegro|Allegro]] is quick and lively, which is clip B.

questions.hint: Tap along with each clip. Which one makes your taps come quicker and quicker?

options.reason: Clip B keeps the same speed from start to finish. The clip that gradually speeds up is clip A: that is [[accelerando|accelerando]].

questions.prompt: What does the word above the first [[bar|bar]] tell you?
questions.hint: Loudness is shown by signs such as *p* and *f*. What else could a word at the very start be about?

options.reason: Loudness is shown by signs such as *p* and *f*. A word above the first [[bar|bar]] names the speed.
Quick and lively is [[allegro|allegro]]. This word is [[andante|andante]], a walking pace.

questions.prompt: Put these words in order, from slowest to fastest.
questions.hint: Start with the slow and calm one. Allegro is quick and lively, so where does it go?

payload.reason: Slowest to fastest: [[adagio|adagio]] slow and calm, [[andante|andante]] walking pace, [[moderato|moderato]] moderate, [[allegro|allegro]] quick and lively.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Accelerando and a tempo are about change. Adagio is about a fixed speed.

left.reason: [[accelerando|Accelerando]] speeds up gradually: it gets faster, not slower.
[[ritardando|Ritardando]] slows down gradually. It is the opposite of accelerando.
[[a-tempo|A tempo]] means return to the speed you had before a change.
[[adagio|Adagio]] is a fixed slow, calm speed, not a change.

questions.prompt: Listen to both clips. Which one is **adagio**?
questions.hint: Adagio is slow and calm. Which clip would you walk to without hurrying?

options.reason: Clip B is quick, about two beats a second. [[adagio|Adagio]] is slow and calm, which is clip A.

questions.prompt: What happens to the speed in this clip?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat at the start. Do your taps have to speed up, slow down, or stay put?

options.reason: The beats get further apart towards the end, so the clip slows down. Speeding up would be [[accelerando|accelerando]].
The speed does not stay put: tap along and your taps have to slow near the end. That is a [[ritardando|ritardando]].

questions.prompt: Which word matches what you hear?
questions.hint: Is the clip speeding up or slowing down? Two of the words mean slowing down.

options.reason: *rit.* is [[ritardando|ritardando]]: gradually slower. The clip speeds up, so it needs *accel.*
*rall.* is [[rallentando|rallentando]], another way to say gradually slower. The clip speeds up, so it needs *accel.*

questions.prompt: Both clips slow down. Which one slows down **a lot**, as *molto rit.* would?
questions.hint: Molto means very much. Which clip ends up much slower than it began?

options.reason: Clip A only eases off a little, which is how *poco rit.* sounds. [[molto|Molto]] means very much, and that is the big slowdown in clip B.

questions.prompt: Which one tells you to slow down gradually?
questions.hint: Two of these are about a change of speed. Only one of them makes the music slower.

options.reason: *accel.* is [[accelerando|accelerando]]: gradually faster. Slowing down is *rit.* or *rall.*
[[allegro|Allegro]] sets a quick, lively speed for the whole piece. It is not a change, and it does not slow the music.

questions.prompt: Put these words in order, from fastest to slowest.
questions.hint: This time start at the quick end. Which word means quick and lively?

payload.reason: Fastest to slowest: [[allegro|allegro]] quick and lively, [[moderato|moderato]] moderate, [[andante|andante]] walking pace, [[adagio|adagio]] slow and calm.

questions.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.hint: Lento is the plainest slow. Rallentando and a tempo are both about change.

left.reason: [[lento|Lento]] means slow, a fixed speed rather than a change.
[[allegretto|Allegretto]] is quite quick, a little slower than allegro.
[[a-tempo|A tempo]] returns to the speed you had before a change.

questions.hint: Molto changes the word after it. Is it a little, or very much?

options.reason: [[poco|Poco]] means a little. [[molto|Molto]] is the opposite: very much, so *molto allegro* is very quick.
Slow and calm is [[adagio|adagio]]. [[allegro|Allegro]] is quick, and [[molto|molto]] makes it even quicker.

questions.prompt: Play the clip. One [[bar|bar]] has a speed word that does not match what you hear. Tap that [[bar|bar]].
questions.hint: Listen to the third [[bar|bar]] of the clip. Does it speed up or slow down?

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 3 says *accel.*, but the music slows down there. It needs *rit.* or *rall.*: gradually slower.

points: Speed words sit above the first [[bar|bar]]. Lento and adagio are slow, andante is a walking pace, moderato is in the middle, allegretto and allegro are quick.
Poco means a little and molto means very much, so molto allegro is very quick.
Accelerando (accel.) means gradually faster. Ritardando (rit.) and rallentando (rall.) mean gradually slower.
A tempo means go back to the speed you had before the change.
